thread:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: KV cache growth detected post-deploy r2028. Continuous batching shows unbounded prefix keys -> memory blowup on inference nodes. Spike in CPU and OOMs across pod group "infer-gpu-pool-2". Correlating with autoscaler thrash. Investigating now.

ash (oncall): I see the same in grafana — mem per pod jumped from ~12GB to 34GB within 3min. 5xx rate up to 2.8% on hosted endpoints. Starting mitigation steps.

karen: tagging severity and paging platform-sre. Are we sure it’s continuous batching config change from the deploy?

mike: rollout r2028 included batching heuristics tweak: continuous_batching.enabled=true and kv.prefix_retention=300s. Reverting those is fastest if confirmed.

lucas: customers impacted: a few production keys reported latency spikes (search-prod, chat-saas-1). Not widespread but noisy.

ash (oncall): quick plan: 1) disable continuous batching cluster-wide on control plane 2) reduce HPA max from 40 -> 10 to stop thrash 3) roll back r2028 if cache still growing after config flip.

ops_kim: Agreed. I'll flip the control-plane flag and patch HPA. Doing step 1 now.

ops_kim: PATCH /admin/config -> {"continuous_batching":false} -> 200 OK. Propagating to regions.

mike: I’m firing an in-place config override for the model serving pods as well: kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/infer-runtime CONT_BATCHING=false --record

ash (oncall): Good. Observability: turning on trace sampling for kv hits to validate we’re no longer accumulating prefixes.

lucas: Noted increase in evictions earlier — kernel OOM traces in node logs. Looks like batch size growth triggered aggressive KV cache retention.

incident-bot: ACTION TAKEN: continuous_batching flag toggled off at control-plane by ops_kim. Notifying HPA controller to stabilize.

ash (oncall): Next step: throttle HPA — patching HPA thresholds to avoid scale-down/up cycles. Running: kubectl patch hpa infer-runtime -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":10,"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":300}}}}'

ops_kim: HPA patched, maxReplicas=10, scaleDown stabilization set to 300s.

karen: Any errors on rollback? If config flip doesn't arrest it we'll revert to r2027.

mike: Initiating quick canary rollback of svc-infer to r2027 in one AZ to verify. Command: ./deploy rollback svc-infer --to r2027 --subset az1

lucas: From logs: KV prefix count slope reduced ~60% after config flip — nice. 5xxs trending down to 0.9% but still above baseline.

ash (oncall): Good signal. Keep watch ~10min. If stable, we’ll keep rollback on standby but hold if metrics continue improving.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: acknowledgement recorded. Current escalation: primary oncall ash acknowledged at 1869000032.

mike: Canary rollback completed for az1 -> r2027. No regression observed so far. Telemetry matches config flip improvements.

ops_kim: Rolling a safety reconnect for prefix eviction job: restarting kv-evictor daemonset to force immediate cleanup. kubectl rollout restart ds/kv-evictor -n redwood

ash (oncall): Evictor restarted. Evictions spike then fall — cache size per pod trending back to baseline.

lucas: Customer impact update: search-prod reported intermittent 500s for ~8 minutes window, root cause appears mitigated. Raising customer post-mortem flag to support team to contact affected accounts.

karen: Nice work. Action items: mike to run post-deploy canary tests for batching heuristics, eng-runtime to add guardrail on prefix retention, infra to add HPA safety cap when continuous batching enabled.

mike: Filed GH issues: 1) runtime: guardrail prefix_retention max 60s #4582 2) deploy: add canary gate for batching toggles #4583

ops_kim: Will follow up with infra HPA changes — adding a feature flag so maxReplicas gets a smaller multiplier while experimental configs are enabled.

ash (oncall): Closing incident once 30m stable. Leaving thread for handoff to next oncall. Next oncall: @karen will lead post-incident review and customer comms.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: continuous batching flip + HPA patch + evictor restart mitigated KV cache blowup. Resolution summary will be generated and attached to ticket RED-INC-2028.

karen: Thanks team. Quick retro tomorrow 10am. :thumbsup:
